key_insight: SpatialEdit-Bench provides the first focused benchmark that jointly measures perceptual plausibility and geometric fidelity for fine-grained, geometry-driven image spatial edits using viewpoint reconstruction and framing analysis.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a standardized, diagnostic evaluation for fine-grained spatial editing where existing models produce perceptually plausible outputs that often fail geometric/layout consistency (object placement, camera viewpoint, framing).
method: Construct SpatialEdit-Bench: curated tasks, paired inputs/targets, and annotations for object layout and camera viewpoint to support fine-grained spatial edits.

Define joint evaluation: perceptual plausibility metrics combined with geometric-fidelity tests (viewpoint reconstruction accuracy and framing analysis) to quantify both appearance and spatial correctness.
Provide evaluation protocols, baseline model runs, and diagnostic analyses to reveal failure modes and guide geometry-aware model development.
impact: Enables standardized, quantitative comparison of spatial-editing methods and steers research toward models that maintain both visual quality and geometric correctness—critical for AR, content creation, and 3D-consistent image synthesis.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing input image + spatial instruction → editor model → edited image, with evaluation modules for perceptual and geometric checks
Before/after example pairs annotated with predicted vs. ground-truth camera/viewpoint arrows and object bounding/layout overlays
Scatter or quadrant chart plotting perceptual score vs. geometric-fidelity score for multiple models to illustrate trade-offs
Gallery of failure modes (misplaced objects, incorrect perspective) alongside metric-driven diagnoses
paper_title: SpatialEdit: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Image Spatial Editing
paper_authors: Yicheng Xiao, Wenhu Zhang, Lin Song, Yukang Chen, Wenbo Li
